questions.question: The memory address of the first element of an array is called

explanations.a: Correct. The memory address of the first element of an array is called the base address, which serves as the reference point for calculating addresses of all other elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Although descriptive, this is not the proper terminology used in programming.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This is not the standard terminology used in computer science for array memory addressing.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While conceptually similar, 'foundation address' is not the correct technical term.

questions.question: The memory allocation for array elements is done

explanations.a: Correct. Array elements are stored in contiguous (consecutive) memory locations, which allows for efficient access using index-based calculations.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Random memory allocation would make it impossible to calculate element addresses using simple mathematical formulas based on indices.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 'Sporadically' is not a technical term for memory allocation.

questions.question: If the memory address of the first element of an array is 2000, what is the memory address of the 6th element?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This calculation doesn't account for the proper size of integer data types.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This would be the address if using a smaller data type or miscalculating the index.
explanations.c: Correct. Assuming 4-byte integers (standard size), the 6th element is at index 5. Using the formula: 2000 + (5 × 4) = 2020.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This would be the address of the 7th element (index 6): 2000 + (6 × 4) = 2024.

questions.question: In C programming, a string is actually a

explanations.a: Correct. In C programming, a string is implemented as an array of characters, terminated by a null character ('\0').
explanations.b: Incorrect. Strings represent text, not numeric values, so they cannot be arrays of integers.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Strings are indeed arrays of characters in C programming.
explanations.d: Incorrect. While a string can be stored in a variable, the underlying data structure is an array of characters, not just a simple variable.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about multidimensional arrays in C is correct?

answers.a: All rows must have the same number of columns.
answers.b: Each row can have a different number of columns.
answers.c: Arrays can only be one-dimensional in C.
answers.d: Arrays in C cannot store integers.

explanations.a: Correct. In C, all rows in a multidimensional array must have the same number of columns.
explanations.b: Incorrect. C does not support jagged arrays as built-in arrays; all rows must have the same number of columns.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Arrays in C can store integers and other data types.

questions.question: Suppose you want to reverse an array of n elements in place. What is the time complexity of this operation?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Reversing an array requires visiting each element at least once.
explanations.b: Incorrect. O(log n) is not sufficient for reversing all elements.
explanations.c: Correct. Each element must be swapped, so the time complexity is O(n).
explanations.d: Incorrect. O(n^2) is not required for reversing an array.
